name: woocommerce
note: WooCommerce catalog portability evolved through the Spike C/D, Grind R1-B/R3-A, and typed-snapshot work documented by the reviewed notes below. The current adapter admits only exact official WooCommerce 11.0.0 and 11.0.1 artifacts (>=11.0.0 <11.0.2), preserves authored simple/variable/grouped/external catalog state and ordered attribute semantics, regenerates independently verifiable native projections, and keeps product deletion fail closed. Official 10.9.4 and the synthetic next-version boundary 11.0.2 are executable refusal controls. No theme range is declared because conformance does not certify a theme-specific dependency.

notes.provider receipt value-level honesty: WooCommerce hierarchy and product-permalink providers declare option:rewrite_rules as the writable durable surface while native rewrite diagnostics are post-action verification evidence. The repair and child paths validate that evidence internally but publish only independently read durable option/lookup projections as before and after; no post-action value may masquerade as a preimage or create a value-level diff. A converged native flush is therefore an honest no-op receipt, while changed or malformed durable state, child/parent disagreement, callback interference, and same-count drift remain blocking. Deterministic full Providers::invoke coverage proves both true pre/post receipts and native durable/effective verification; candidate-bound hierarchy/rewrite action apply plus recapture exercise the engine contract.
notes.canonical mixed-option object contracts: Mixed option sub_keys are JSON objects, so insertion order is not semantic and compiled artifacts recursively sort their keys. The WooCommerce interpreter compares canonical contract bytes rather than PHP associative-array order while retaining the exact closed key set and each authored/env rule. A reordered exact admin-payment email contract normalizes identically; a missing, extra, or differently classified sibling still refuses with the bounded contract diagnostic.
notes.inactive-target local-pickup cost compil: Deploy compiles the immutable repository before it activates canonical plugins, so the WooCommerce interpreter cannot require wc_format_decimal() merely to validate local-pickup cost bytes. Exact official 11.0.0 and 11.0.1 carry byte-identical includes/wc-formatting-functions.php (sha256 c3576416420bbfb6893ad5164ccf8c439b7e731c337c04b32e058ac6a0809d41). The digest-bound interpreter now validates that closed grammar directly, without copying Woo rounding behavior or consulting target options, locale, filters, or inactive plugin code. Empty cost retains the native no-charge meaning; plus signs, exponent notation, localized separators, whitespace, currency text, multiple signs/dots, controls, and over-1024-byte values remain blocking. Deterministic readiness covers the accepted and rejected grammar with wc_format_decimal absent, while exact-artifact conformance covers active native REST capture, inactive-target deploy compilation, activation, apply, rate calculation, and byte-identical recapture.
notes.local pickup REST records (supersedes th: Exact WooCommerce 11.0.0 and 11.0.1 carry byte-identical Settings REST, ShippingController, PickupLocation, LocalPickupUtils, WC_Settings_API, WC_Shipping_Method, WC_Shipping_Rate, and decimal-calculation sources. Safe inline HTML in both name and details must already equal wp_kses_post bytes, and a nonempty cost must already equal Woo's wc_format_decimal calculation bytes. Wrong scalar types, noncanonical text/HTML/decimal values, controls, oversize values, and object-bearing serialization refuse with bounded diagnostics. ShippingController attaches WC_Cache_Helper's shipping-version refresh to the pre-update hook for each option; Duo's direct SQL path selects the existing receipt-bound woocommerce-cache action for both exact triggers. Repository tests cover every settings subset, Unicode/RTL/HTML, empty/delete, malformed, unknown, secret-shaped, count/byte bounds, and both trigger selections; live conformance writes through /wp/v2/settings and reads through that REST route, LocalPickupUtils, PickupLocation, and WC_Shipping_Rate. The machine inventory binds the exact read/write/render/calculation sources and both official artifact hashes. Coming-soon state retains its target-owned boundary; gateway/email records use the separate digest-bound closed-subkey contract, and thumbnail controls are separately closed by the superseding request-time convergence contract.
notes.thumbnail image settings and request-tim: Exact official WooCommerce 11.0.0 and 11.0.1 carry byte-identical Customizer, wc_get_image_size(), WC_Regenerate_Images, background-request, WC_Post_Data, REST/Store API image-schema, and product-image sources. woocommerce_thumbnail_cropping, its two custom ratio controls, and the pre-existing woocommerce_thumbnail_image_width are ordinary authored storefront choices. Repository bytes must be the exact UI-native cropping enum or canonical absint strings; dimensions and the resulting custom projection are bounded before apply. The Customizer-only maybe_regenerate_images() hash and attachment background queue are target runtime accelerators, not authored state: every normal frontend, REST, and Store API thumbnail crosses the always-registered image_get_intermediate_size and wp_get_attachment_image_src callbacks. A stale ratio synchronously generates only the requested Woo size and updates metadata. Missing attachment metadata or source-file preconditions preserve the prior image and metadata so the next request retries. On the evidenced normal 800-by-600 JPEG path with no scale, format conversion, or EXIF rotation, WordPress 7.1 writes base metadata (file, width, height, filesize, sizes=[]) before subsize editor selection. An unavailable subsize editor therefore returns the bounded full image with that base metadata persisted, and the next request regenerates the requested Woo derivative. Earlier editor use for WordPress scale, conversion, or EXIF paths remains native target behavior rather than part of this claim. A same-ratio pixel-width change uses WordPress's native closest/full-size fallback with output dimensions constrained to the requested size, while a smaller original remains unscaled exactly as native Woo intends. Queue absence, cancellation, and multisite therefore do not change authored-option semantics. Attachment metadata, derivative files, and the regeneration hash/queue remain derived or runtime; external Photon/CDN processors remain target-environment-owned. Deterministic product-path regressions bind defaults, absence/delete, custom/uncropped and 300-to-500 transitions, same/fresh reads, failure/retry/idempotence, bounds, malformed values, and the exact Woo callback identities; final candidate-bound live evidence runs those callbacks without stubbing them away.
notes.analytics and stock-retention scheduler: Exact WooCommerce 11.0.0 and 11.0.1 carry byte-identical OrdersScheduler, scheduler-trait, customer-stock DataRetentionController, Action Scheduler schema, and logger-schema sources. The authored woocommerce_analytics_scheduled_import yes/no setting selects a scoped provider that fences the exact wc-admin-data action family, binds a versioned non-autoloaded intent to the current scoped operation, reproduces Woo's no-to-yes cursor reset only for a proved transition, and converges recurring or one-time catch-up topology without rescheduling a naturally consumed catch-up. It validates bounded raw action bytes before native hydration, exact InnoDB columns and indexes including prefix widths, DBStore singleton claim state, option/autoload bytes, every crossed hook, exact container-owned callback identities, claim preimages, transaction ambiguity, and exhaustive mutex/claim release. The authored stock-notification retention threshold accepts absence/empty or canonical whole days through 3650000 only with the native alpha feature enabled; repair row-locks the bounded whole cron option, preserves every unrelated event byte, refuses external-cache publication, and proves exact daily horizon/cardinality. Scoped reconcile is read-only. Crash/rollback/retry, same-length drift, concurrent connections, worker claims, foreign topology, malformed schema/index/serialization, hook injection, marker provenance/autoload, lifecycle residue, redacted diagnostics, and both exact artifact digests are deterministic offline regressions. The marker and Woo cursors remain target-runtime state, and every table, option, and native frontier touched by either capability is declared in the rollback inventory.

notes.initial taxonomy scope (DUO-3336): WooCommerce's registered taxonomy names do not all have the same portability semantics. Merchant-authored catalog categories, tags, shipping classes, product-type relationships, featured/catalog visibility intent, and POS visibility intent are explicit authored declarations so a generic initializer can widen policy only from adapter-owned facts. The product_visibility relationship is mixed: provider v3 preserves authored featured/catalog intent while regenerating target-local outofstock/rated-* terms from fresh native product state. pos_product_visibility carries the authored pos-hidden choice only for non-downloadable simple/variable roots and requires exact variation inheritance. Dynamic pa_* attribute taxonomies continue through taxonomy_patterns. These rulings belong here, never in generic init or capture branches.
notes.shipping/tax typed-row deletion cache bo: Typed shipping-zone/method and tax-rate/location creation and update are portable, and the generic synthetic deletion contract exercises child ordering, option-name guards, and cache inventory. The shipped Woo adapter deliberately grants no deletion authority for these rows: Woo CRUD/API effects, extension reverse references, and every persistent-cache consequence are not a closed semantic-delete contract. Exact WooCommerce 11.0.0/11.0.1 expose WC_Cache_Helper::invalidate_cache_group() for the woocommerce-attributes, shipping_zones, and taxes groups plus WC_Cache_Helper::get_transient_version('shipping', true); the mandatory fresh-process rebuilder invokes those version-pinned boundaries after supported writes. notes.product.modified_timestamps (post fields: WooCommerce's product and variation CRUD saves update wp_posts.post_modified and post_modified_gmt as persistence timestamps even when the authored product inputs are unchanged (the ecommerce run observed this after target-only stock saves). These front-matter fields remain captured verbatim for operator visibility and are still written as starting values when Duo creates a row, but are classified derived for product and product_variation so Canon's hash basis ignores timestamp-only differences and Apply preserves the target's existing timestamps instead of replaying stale source times. This declaration is intentionally scoped to Woo products and variations; every undeclared post type keeps authored timestamp semantics.

notes.whole-core operational option union: The visible Settings screens are not the whole option surface. A second exact 11.0.0/11.0.1 source pass freezes 105 residual Woo-prefixed literals across 80 option readers, writers, deleters, settings APIs, setup/onboarding flows, and migrations. One normal merchant product control, woocommerce_product_type, is authored and restricted to the four exact core types through the V4 REST authority. Sixteen deployment/service/onboarding choices remain target environment state; seventy-seven cursors, notices, UI progress rows, migration residues, obsolete page/slug aliases, remote caches, and telemetry records remain target runtime; three bounded generated families cover only core notice/install workflow state. The bare concatenation fragments receive no authority. The machine inventory binds the sorted classification bytes, exact category counts, both artifact hashes, the 78 shared source bytes, and the two version-specific source files so a future normal core literal cannot disappear behind a default-only fixture.
notes.product_lookup_regeneration: DUO-3411 narrows the provider certified against exact WooCommerce 11.0.0/11.0.1 to surfaces with stable public synthesis and independent value readback. Simple and variation active prices are selected through WC_Product::is_on_sale(edit), get_sale_price(edit), and get_regular_price(edit); variable and grouped roots use the public sync_price() stores while a narrowly scoped WordPress delete_post_metadata filter preserves repository-authored parent regular/sale rows. wc_product_meta_lookup is refreshed through refresh_product_lookup_table() and verified by comparing WooCommerce's published lookup derivation with the stored SQL row; bounded sale actions use Woo's public scheduling helpers with exact readback. Both admitted artifacts expose the public synchronous ProductAttributesLookup\LookupDataStore::create_data_for_product() writer and get_last_create_operation_failed() status. The provider invokes that writer once per deduplicated live product root, removes tombstoned product/root rows synchronously instead of leaving Woo's public asynchronous deletion action pending, and binds the exact sorted six-column scoped table rows into its receipt. Root-owned chunking prevents the same variation row being observed twice when a batch crosses 200 ids, while duplicate stored rows, equal-count drift, writer failure, and delete failure all remain loud and retryable. Scoped receipts bind every selected lookup value, sale timestamp, downloadable-file locator, and product-attribute row with non-disclosing SHA-256 fingerprints so same-count drift cannot retire recovery. Product and variation entity deletion remain unsupported; the deletion path here only converges this derived table when a future authorized engine channel supplies a tombstone. The provider stays digest-bound through the manifest providers declaration and consumes the same deletion, reparent, retry, and always-on-write engine channels established by DUO-3342.
notes.download approval projection (WooCommerc: WooCommerce 11.0.x (verified at exact 11.0.0 and 11.0.1) hydrates every _downloadable_files row through WC_Product_Download::check_is_valid(), which disables a file when its rebased target parent is absent from the target-local wc_product_download_directories register. Duo writes postmeta with SQL, so the native administrator save that normally adds this rule never runs. Provider v2 repairs only the finite product/product_variation ids selected by the current apply: it reads their fresh raw metadata through Duo's class-disabled PlainData boundary before any object hook can execute, accepts only Woo core's id/name/file/enabled row schema, rejects disabled and shortcode/extension-executed locators, delegates parent normalization and containment to WooCommerce's version-pinned ApprovedDirectories Register and URL APIs, preserves all unrelated and broader target rules, additively enables only the exact missing parent needed by an authored enabled download, and then requires both Register::is_valid_path() and a fresh WC_Product::get_downloads() read to expose the exact key cardinality plus id, name, file, and enabled state. Receipts contain counts and a SHA-256 scope binding, never URLs, query strings, names, or ids. Removed or changed downloads do not delete old target rules, matching WooCommerce's own additive registry semantics. The table stays runtime for capture: this provider derives only the minimum target projection required by the authored product batch rather than copying a source security registry.
notes.category and brand hierarchy projection: Exact WooCommerce 11.0.0 and 11.0.1 expose the byte-identical public whole-taxonomy CategoryLookup::regenerate() boundary while keeping row-level update/delete protected. The manifest-owned hierarchy provider therefore launches a clean WP-CLI child after product_cat or product_brand writes, explicitly invalidates persistent terms, term-query, taxonomy, and option caches, deletes and natively regenerates both WordPress *_children options, then calls Woo's public whole-category regenerator. The child independently derives the exact ancestor closure and canonical child maps from current term parents and emits only counts/hashes; the parent re-reads checked raw option bytes, effective option values, and every sorted category table row and requires exact fingerprint agreement. Authored parent fingerprints/counts (plus the brand permalink fingerprint on the rewrite path) must remain identical across the child, so a concurrent source edit cannot be blessed even when both readbacks agree. Parent and lookup reads carry exact MAX+1 limits, graph validation is linear, and category closure refuses above 200000 rows before allocation. Same-count stale maps/rows, missing rows, malformed graphs, schema drift, child warnings, failure, and post-child races remain loud and retryable. A separate action reuses that fresh-process sequence for authored woocommerce_brand_permalink changes and then performs a soft native rewrite flush, requiring stored raw/effective rewrite rules to match a second fresh native generation. Exact cache/hook/DB effects are declared for checkpoint/recovery.
notes.product_effect_provider_resource (WooCom: The product and product_variation regenerator's irreversible provider-resource aggregate is deliberately explicit: WooCommerce 11.0.x (verified at exact 11.0.0 and 11.0.1) can mutate or read cache keys in the `product_<id>` and `object_<id>` groups, the `products` group, the `product_objects` ProductCache group (introduced in 10.5), and product-specific transients. The transient family is `wc_product_children_<id>`, `wc_var_prices_<id>`, `wc_related_<id>`, `wc_child_has_weight_<id>`, and `wc_child_has_dimensions_<id>`; fixed product transients (`wc_products_onsale`, `wc_featured_products`, `wc_outofstock_count`, `wc_low_stock_count`) are also cleared by ProductUtil. No bounded provider inverse or fresh readback exists, so this remains an irreversible blocker. The exact product callback boundaries are separately declared as irreversible hooks: `woocommerce_product_read` (CPT data-store read), `woocommerce_delete_product_transients` (ProductUtil after transient cleanup), and `woocommerce_updated_product_price` (variable data-store sync_price). Product and variation effect IDs are intentionally distinct even when they name the same Woo callback or aggregate resource.
notes.attribute/shipping transient callback bo: The attribute-taxonomy transient delete command can invoke WordPress's exact `delete_transient_wc_attribute_taxonomies` callback and the post-success `deleted_transient` action; both are irreversible in the inventory. The shipping version invalidator calls `get_transient('shipping-transient-version')` and then `set_transient()`; its exact WordPress filter/action surfaces are declared (`pre_transient_shipping-transient-version`, `transient_shipping-transient-version`, `pre_set_transient_shipping-transient-version`, `expiration_of_transient_shipping-transient-version`, `set_transient_shipping-transient-version`, `set_transient`, and the 6.8-deprecated `setted_transient`). The command immediately performs a non-refresh read and requires byte-identical version output, so a successful refresh return by itself is not treated as persistence proof. `wc_delete_attribute()`'s `woocommerce_before_attribute_delete`, `woocommerce_attribute_deleted`, and scheduled `woocommerce_flush_rewrite_rules` are intentionally omitted: typed attribute deletion is unsupported and the raw snapshot path invokes none of those Woo APIs. Likewise `WC_Shipping_Zone::add_shipping_method()`'s `woocommerce_shipping_zone_method_added` is omitted because this adapter's typed shipping-row path does not call Woo's shipping CRUD setter; the declared effects cover only callbacks the shipped command/path can actually invoke.
notes.late attribute taxonomy registration cal: The product provider's post-init taxonomy repair reads `woocommerce_permalinks` and reproduces Woo 11.0.x's option-write-free default/rewrite-base projection without calling `wc_get_permalink_structure()`, because that helper can persist normalized defaults and would make an unrelated option write part of product repair. The generic `pre_option` filter plus fixed `pre_option_woocommerce_permalinks`, `option_woocommerce_permalinks`, and `default_option_woocommerce_permalinks` read filters are declared for both product trigger halves. Woo's dynamic `woocommerce_taxonomy_objects_pa_<attribute>` and `woocommerce_taxonomy_args_pa_<attribute>` callbacks are represented by the exact irreversible provider-owned filter-family resource `woocommerce-attribute-taxonomy-registration-filters:v1`. It deliberately does not use the engine-owned `{slug}` member grammar: WooCommerce 11.0.x (verified at exact 11.0.0 and 11.0.1) permits byte-limited multibyte attribute slugs, while `{slug}` is an ASCII core identifier. The resource remains bounded to these two provider-invoked, version-pinned filter families without teaching generic engine code a Woo taxonomy alphabet or silently excluding a valid callback name.
notes._low_stock_amount: Per-product low-stock threshold override reads like a runtime signal (it's stock-adjacent) but it's a merchant-set policy value, not something WooCommerce derives or recomputes — classified authored deliberately rather than lumped in with _stock/_stock_status.
notes._price: REVISED in Grind R1-B and DUO-3411 — _price is derived, not authored. WooCommerce computes it from regular/sale/date inputs; variable products additionally store one _price row per distinct child price, so Capture's single-valued authored-meta contract cannot own it. The version-pinned provider now asks WooCommerce's public is_on_sale/edit and price accessors to select simple/variation active values, uses public variable/grouped sync_price() for parent ranges, preserves authored parent regular/sale rows through a narrowly scoped WordPress metadata-deletion filter, independently verifies wc_product_meta_lookup, and regenerates/binds exact scoped wc_product_attributes_lookup rows through WooCommerce's public synchronous data store. Runtime stock/order fields remain target-local.
notes._used_by: Every coupon redemption adds a NEW postmeta row via add_post_meta() (never update) — one row per use, value = lowercased user id or guest billing email (class-wc-coupon-data-store-cpt.php add_coupon_used_by()). This is exactly the multi-value-authored-meta shape v0's engine refuses (Capture.php throws on >1 row for an 'authored' key) — classifying it runtime is not just correct (it's redemption history, not merchant-authored config) but is what keeps capture from throwing on any coupon that's ever been used. Confirmed empirically: redeeming a coupon on env A adds a `_used_by` row and increments `usage_count`; neither must propagate to env B on apply (runtime isolation).
notes._children: Grouped product's member simple products (WC_Product_Grouped::set_children()). Confirmed empirically as a real serialized PHP array of ints keyed by sequential integer index — `a:2:{i:0;i:15;i:1;i:16;}` — not a CSV string like product_ids and not string-cast like _crosssell_ids/_upsell_ids: ref post[] with no cast, the plain int[] shape (same declared shape as product_categories, just pointing at posts instead of terms). Lint's bare_id check is exactly what catches an accidental omission of the ref declaration here — verified live during this manifest's authoring: dropping `ref: post[]` and recapturing produced two real bare_id findings naming the actual child products by title, restoring the declaration made lint clean again on the same recapture.
notes._default_attributes: Variable product's pre-selected variation, one entry per used-for-variation attribute (WC_Product_Variable::set_default_attributes()). Confirmed empirically: `a:2:{s:7:"pa_size";s:5:"small";s:8:"pa_color";s:3:"red";}` — keyed by the attribute's TAXONOMY NAME (`pa_size`, a string, stable across environments by construction) with the value being the term SLUG (also a stable string), never a term_id. Classified authored, no ref — there is no numeric id anywhere in this value to rewrite; a slug is exactly as portable as the option/meta keys that already round-trip without tokenization.
notes._product_attributes: Every product's (simple or variable) attribute assignment table (WC_Product::set_attributes(), always present once any attribute is added, even a single custom/local one). Confirmed empirically for a variable product using GLOBAL (taxonomy) attributes: `a:2:{s:7:"pa_size";a:6:{s:4:"name";s:7:"pa_size";s:5:"value";s:0:"";s:8:"position";i:0;s:10:"is_visible";i:1;s:12:"is_variation";i:1;s:11:"is_taxonomy";i:1;}...}` — `value` is the empty string for every is_taxonomy=1 entry; the actual term assignment lives in the ordinary term_relationships under the pa_* taxonomy (captured through the generic taxonomy machinery once pa_size/pa_color are in policy.taxonomies scope — see the pa_* note below), not in this meta value at all. A LOCAL (non-global, product-specific) attribute would instead put its option list directly in `value` as a pipe-separated string of free text (e.g. `Cotton | Wool`) — still no numeric ids, just prose the merchant typed. Either shape is plain, ref-free data: classified authored with no ref/json_refs declaration. (Scope note: this manifest's shop only exercises the taxonomy/global-attribute shape; the local-attribute pipe-string shape is documented here from WooCommerce's own known behavior, not independently re-verified in this round — flagged rather than silently assumed.)
notes._variation_description: Per-variation description field (WC_Product_Variation), written unconditionally on every variation create/update — even to an empty string, so it hits the classification gate on the very first variable product a site ever gets, not just ones that use it. Plain text, classified authored, no ref.
notes.product_variation.title (fields, task #8: post_title is a POST FIELD (one of the ~13 keys Capture::build_post()/Apply::finalize_post() hardcode into every post's front matter unconditionally), not post_meta/options — until task #88 there was no manifest hook to classify one at all. Root cause, confirmed via WooCommerce's own source and empirically reproduced on the r1b pair (task #72): WC_Product_Variation_Data_Store_CPT::read() recomputes a variation's title from the PARENT's _product_attributes order plus the variation's own current attribute values on EVERY wc_get_product() load, writing the result via a raw $wpdb->update() specifically to dodge wp_update_post()/save_post (WooCommerce's own code comment: avoiding an infinite loop) — hook-free, invisible to Apply's canary, no post_modified bump. Two environments that have received a different number/timing of ordinary WooCommerce-mediated reads (an admin view, a Store API request, a wc-cli command) can therefore transiently hold different title BYTES for the identical variation while every authored input (parent title, attribute assignments — both already captured/applied correctly) is byte-identical on both sides; they converge to the same self-healed value once each has had at least one such read, because the computed value depends only on that already-portable data, nothing environment-local. Declared here as {"class": "derived"} under this post_type's new "fields" key (Policy::field_class(), analogous to this same object's existing "body"/"phase" keys) — the evidence-backed allowlist now covers 'title', 'modified', and 'modified_gmt' for Woo product types; Policy validates each field name/class at manifest-load time and throws on anything else, so slug (which participates in file NAMES and collision/identity checks, not just content) and status/post_date/post_date_gmt/menu_order/comment_status/ping_status/excerpt (no proven self-healing or target-owned timestamp precedent) stay unsupported rather than half-supported. Semantics, argued explicitly since task #88 left both open as valid: Capture keeps writing the field's CURRENT observed value into the file verbatim, every time, exactly like any other front-matter field — never silently omitted, so a human reading state/ always sees what each field actually is right now. Apply's phase-1 insert still writes captured derived values as a brand-new row's starting values (no rebuilder exists to conjure one the way _wp_attachment_metadata gets one, and WordPress requires SOME value on insert) — but phase-2 finalize_post() now excludes each declared derived field from its UPDATE statement entirely once the row exists, rather than overwriting it with the captured byte string on every apply. Chosen over always-write: always-write would make a target environment's own, more-progressed self-heal regress to a stale source snapshot on every apply cycle, only to re-heal itself on the very next ordinary WooCommerce read — a pointless oscillation for a value nothing authored actually controls; letting the plugin's own derivation stand once the row exists is what 'derived' means for a field with no rebuilder. Separately — and this is the half that actually closes the gap rather than relabeling it — Canon::post_hash_basis() excludes every field a post_type classifies derived from the representation that gets HASHED for Ledger's duo_state, Apply::build_plan()'s three-way compare, and Capture::snapshot()'s env view (Capture::run()/snapshot() and Apply::load_tree() all hash this basis now, not the raw file bytes, for posts), so title/timestamp-only divergence is structurally invisible to plan/drift/conflict detection, not merely excluded from one test's diff. sandbox/tests/grind/grind_r1b_shop.sh proves both halves on the real Duo Tee fixture: an explicit 'duo plan' assertion that a title-only self-heal on one side alone never appears in drift/update/conflict, and — since capture still records the CURRENT value verbatim, so two environments at genuinely different self-heal moments would still show different file bytes — a forced, real wc_get_product() read (WooCommerce's own natural mechanism, not a duo mechanism, run outside any apply/capture window, the same read any admin product-list view or Store API request triggers naturally) on every variation on both sides before the final byte-identity assertion, which now asserts TRUE identity with the NON_TITLE_DIFFS exclusion removed entirely and passes because both sides converge to the identical WooCommerce-computed value off byte-identical authored inputs.

notes.attribute_pa_* (meta_patterns): Every USED-FOR-VARIATION global attribute mints a variation-level postmeta key named `attribute_<taxonomy>` (`attribute_pa_size`, `attribute_pa_color`, ...) — the taxonomy name is dynamic (one per merchant-created attribute; see the pa_* note below), so a static post_meta entry can never cover a site's full attribute set, only whichever attributes existed when the manifest was last edited. Confirmed empirically the value is always the term SLUG as a plain string (`small`, `red`) — portable, no numeric id, no ref needed — so `meta_patterns: [{"match": "^attribute_pa_", "class": "authored"}]` covers every past and future global attribute in one declaration with zero risk (the value shape never contains a ref regardless of which attribute the key names). notes.pa_* attribute taxonomies (dynamic taxon: SUPERSEDED by task #92's taxonomy_patterns entry below — this note is kept verbatim as the empirical trail that motivated it, not deleted (this project's convention: append, don't erase history). WooCommerce mints a taxonomy per global attribute at runtime — `wc_attribute_taxonomy_name()` returns `'pa_' . sanitize_title($attribute->attribute_name)` (truncated+hashed past 27 chars) — registered on `init` by reading `wp_woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies` (a custom table, see the tables section below), NOT declared anywhere in code. This manifest cannot list pa_size/pa_color the way manifests/core.json lists category/post_tag: every NEW global attribute a merchant creates is a taxonomy this manifest has never heard of. Confirmed empirically what actually happens: (1) TERM data (the taxonomy's own terms — Small/Medium/Large, Red/Blue/Black — and a product's term_relationships under that taxonomy) flows through the EXISTING generic taxonomy-capture machinery with ZERO new engine code, exactly like category/product_cat, the moment the taxonomy's bare name is added to site.duo.json's policy.taxonomies array — proving the generic terms path is genuinely attribute-agnostic. (2) Policy::taxonomies() (agent/src/Policy/Policy.php) returns that array as a flat, exact-string list with NO pattern/wildcard fallback — unlike options and post_meta/term_meta, taxonomies has no PATTERN_KEYS entry at all (confirmed by reading Policy::rule()'s pattern-fallback code, which is keyed off a fixed PATTERN_KEYS map that only has 'options' and 'post_meta'/'term_meta'). So while attribute_pa_* POST META was solvable with one meta_patterns line (see above), the TAXONOMY SCOPE LIST has no equivalent: every new global attribute needs a manual, human site.duo.json edit adding its exact pa_<name> string, forever — there is no manifest-level fix available in this engine for taxonomies the way there is for meta keys. (3) The sharper failure is on the TARGET environment, not the source: pa_size/pa_color's very existence as registered taxonomies depends on rows in the woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies custom table, which nothing in this engine captures or applies (see the tables note) — so on a fresh environment that has never had that attribute created through its own admin/wp-cli, `get_taxonomy('pa_size')` returns false. Capture.php's own taxes_by_object_type() already anticipates exactly this ('a scoped taxonomy that isn't registered at runtime... is excluded entirely and named in a loud warning') for the CAPTURE side; empirically, applying pa_size/pa_color TERM entities via `duo apply` on such an environment is the sharper, unguarded case — term insertion itself calls WordPress's own wp_insert_term()/taxonomy APIs, which behave unpredictably (silently registering an ad hoc, config-less taxonomy row, or failing) against a taxonomy WooCommerce itself doesn't know exists yet, because nothing upstream of that call ever re-created the woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies row that would have registered it for real. The empirically-verified, honest mitigation for this grind round: PRE-PROVISION every global attribute (`wp wc product_attribute create` — the same real, admin-facing action used to create it originally) on every target environment BEFORE the first apply that references its terms, exactly the same operational discipline this sandbox already uses for WooCommerce/Storefront themselves (installed independently on both environments, never propagated through the site repo's code/ tree). This is a manual step, not an automated one — grind round R1-B's acceptance criteria for a real typed-snapshot implementation of woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies were exactly 'zero manual pre-provisioning step', and the task #75 graduation note below is what satisfies them.
notes.taxonomy_patterns (task #92, closes the: Two mechanisms compose to close zero-provisioning: task #75's woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies typed-snapshot (already shipped) makes the ATTRIBUTE TABLE ROW itself travel — confirmed live by r3-eng-fields validating #88 on r1b2: right after a `duo apply` that lands a new attribute row, `get_taxonomy('pa_size')`/`get_taxonomy('pa_color')` both return true in the NEXT fresh wp-cli process, zero manual steps. What #75 alone does NOT fix is (a) the taxonomy SCOPE LIST (site.duo.json still needed pa_size/pa_color listed by hand — Policy::taxonomies() had no pattern fallback) and (b) relationship-writing correctness WITHIN the SAME apply request that lands a brand-new attribute (WooCommerce registers pa_* taxonomies by reading its table on `init`, which already ran before Snapshot's phase-1 write of that table's row this request — reproduced directly, not just reasoned about: a raw-SQL insert into wp_woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies leaves get_taxonomy() returning false for the REST of that same PHP process, even though a paired raw-SQL term_taxonomy row for the new taxonomy name is immediately visible to a live `SELECT DISTINCT taxonomy FROM wp_term_taxonomy` in the identical process). taxonomy_patterns closes both: Policy::taxonomies() now expands the exact policy.taxonomies list with every live wp_term_taxonomy name matching a declared pattern (scope-gated — never a blanket widen, only pattern-matched names are ever added), and the declared `object_type` here is consulted ONLY as a fallback when get_taxonomy() fails, letting direct-SQL term-relationship writes correctly scope a just-landed pa_* taxonomy without needing WordPress's runtime registry to have caught up. `object_type: ["product"]` is sourced from WooCommerce's actual current code (fetched directly, not recalled): class-wc-post-types.php's register_taxonomies() calls `register_taxonomy($name, apply_filters("woocommerce_taxonomy_objects_{$name}", array('product')), ...)` — the literal, unfiltered default for every pa_* taxonomy. With both mechanisms in place, site.duo.json no longer needs pa_size/pa_color listed at all — the whole point of zero manual provisioning.

THE OPTION-NAME MECHANISM (option_name_refs, closing the third compounding problem the note above named): a new manifest section, sibling to option_patterns (not nested inside `tables` — every other section is an independently-mergeable top-level sibling; nesting would be the only cross-section nesting in the whole grammar and would misplace the concept, since an option's relationship to an id_kind is the same shape as an ordinary `options` ref rule's relationship to the post/term keyspace). `match` is a regex with a required named group `id` marking the ref-bearing segment — anchored `^...$`, tested live against real option names on this install including two genuine false-positive risks (woocommerce_paypal_settings, woocommerce_maxmind_geolocation_settings, both matching a naive `*_settings` search but correctly EXCLUDED by this regex since neither ends in a digit run before `_settings`). Capture::build_options() runs one full option-NAME scan (names only) per capture and tests each against every declared pattern — a new discovery mechanism, since Policy::authored_options() is exact-whitelist-only and never consults option_patterns for discovery at all (confirmed by reading it directly, and matches this task's own prior characterization). The captured KEY splices the resolved ref TOKEN into the id segment's exact byte position (e.g. `woocommerce_flat_rate_{{wc_zone_method:<uuid>}}_settings`) using the SAME `{{kind:uuid}}` grammar every other ref already uses — Tokens::id_to_token()/token_to_id() needed zero changes, confirmed already generic over any declared id_kind. Apply detects a token-bearing option KEY before its ordinary option-rule dispatch (unconditionally, not gated) — confirmed this ordering is load-bearing, not cosmetic: skipping it would silently write a REAL wp_options row whose NAME contains literal '{{...}}' bytes to the target, not a crash. Severity model (team-lead design review, mirroring task #73's dangling-vs-unscoped split): an embedded id resolving to no row anywhere is ordinary dangling (warn+drop); an embedded id naming a row that genuinely EXISTS in its declared table but was never minted a uuid (e.g. the table isn't pinned as authored_snapshot) is unscoped (loud, blocking, `--force-unresolved-refs` escape hatch — Snapshot::row_exists_for_kind() is the new helper this distinction needed). Settings VALUES route through struct_capture()/struct_apply() unconditionally (not gated on json_refs/key_refs being declared, unlike ordinary options) specifically so an array-shaped settings blob (title/cost/tax_status for flat_rate; title/min_amount for free_shipping — both confirmed live, plain scalars, no ids) gets its string leaves URL-tokenized with zero per-method-id special-casing; deliberately NOT the same default as ordinary build_options() (which leaves an untouched array value alone unless json_refs/key_refs is declared) — this is a new, narrower path scoped only to option_name_refs rows, so it doesn't risk a behavior change to already-shipped manifests. Secret guard: Secrets::hard_match_deep() (not the shallow is_string() check the ordinary options loop uses, which would silently never scan an array's own string leaves — caught during this task's own design review before any code shipped, before it could become a real gap) — verified live against both real fixtures (flat_rate, free_shipping settings, both null/clean) AND a deliberately-planted fake Stripe key nested in the same array shape (correctly caught), proving the guard actually works.

notes.woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies natural: attribute_name is the declared natural_key bootstrap column and row slug. A never-seen row derives UUIDv5 from `woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies:<attribute_name>`; after first capture, Duo consults duo_map first, so a WooCommerce attribute slug rename is an ordinary update/file rename that retains the existing UUID. UUIDv5(current attribute_name) differing from that retained UUID is expected after a rename and is reported as an informational capture/plan note; Duo never forces re-derivation. WooCommerce's `wp wc product_attribute update --name=<label>` may regenerate attribute_name when `--slug` is omitted, and that rename still retains identity when ledger continuity exists. A fresh environment independently capturing the already-renamed row with neither ledger nor repository history derives UUIDv5 from the new slug and therefore gets a different UUID; existing table adopt flows are the reconciliation path for that documented bootstrap/continuity boundary.
notes.woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies deletio: Deletion is deliberately unsupported: this manifest MUST NOT declare `table:woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies` in `deletions` until the engine can model WooCommerce's semantic delete. Re-read and live-probed against WooCommerce 11.0.0: `wc_delete_attribute()` derives `pa_<attribute_name>`, deletes the definition row, deletes every taxonomy term through `wp_delete_term()` (thereby removing term_taxonomy/term_relationship rows and possibly the term), fires `woocommerce_attribute_deleted`, schedules `woocommerce_flush_rewrite_rules`, deletes the `wc_attribute_taxonomies` transient, and invalidates the `woocommerce-attributes` object-cache group; registered taxonomy state changes only in a fresh process. Woo's hooks also invalidate product/variation version strings and regenerate variation summaries. A real variable-product probe showed Woo intentionally leaves `_product_attributes`, `attribute_pa_<slug>`, and `wc_product_attributes_lookup` rows behind, while Duo's generic raw table delete plus the existing transient rebuilder additionally leaves the taxonomy terms and relationships behind and fires none of those hooks. The reverse references are derived strings or serialized/key-shaped data (`term_taxonomy.taxonomy`, `_product_attributes`, variation meta keys, and lookup-table `taxonomy`), so v1 deletion guards—which compare a target UUID's numeric ledger id to one scalar column—cannot represent them. Table cascades only model declared attached-meta sidecars and cannot invoke Woo's API-level effects. The loud missing-capability refusal is therefore the safe contract; `--with-deletes` and `--force-delete-referenced` do not bypass it. See `sandbox/tests/live/regress_woo_attribute_deletion.sh`.
notes.product deletion boundary (DUO-3225): Product deletion is deliberately unsupported in the exact WooCommerce 11.0.0/11.0.1 contract. The former post:product capability guarded core comments, child posts, and wc_order_product_lookup, but that was not a closed reverse-reference inventory: downloadable permissions, subscription extensions, payment/order-item metadata, and arbitrary extension custom tables can reference a product through scalar, meta, serialized, or plugin-owned keyspaces. A broad compatibility claim cannot prove those absent, and forcing the old guard could leave a live order or extension record orphaned. The manifest therefore declares no post:product deletion capability. Capture/plan/apply refuse product tombstones before mutation, and neither --with-deletes nor --force-delete-referenced broadens authority. This is the issue's explicit supported-subset reduction: authored product creation/update is certified; product deletion requires an adapter-specific semantic delete contract in a future version.
notes.flagship closure (DUO-3225/DUO-3411): The adapter certified against exact WooCommerce 11.0.0/11.0.1 owns the independently verifiable product-meta lookup, effective-price, attribute-lookup, category/brand hierarchy, cache, sale-schedule, and mixed visibility surfaces. It does not reproduce WooCommerce price or attribute-row business rules: public Woo price APIs own price selection/synchronization, the public synchronous ProductAttributesLookup data store owns exact scoped attribute-row regeneration, and public CategoryLookup owns the whole-taxonomy category closure. Independent checked raw-table/option fingerprints prevent equal-count drift from satisfying receipts. Conformance covers supported price/meta/sale/attribute/hierarchy/visibility behavior plus Store API and cart behavior without presenting Store API filtering as a raw table oracle. Woo product/variation entity deletion remains an explicit boundary.
notes.Woo 11.0.x product, term, and optional-c: Exact official 11.0.0 and 11.0.1 source has byte-identical writers/readers for external-product `_product_url`/`_button_text`, product and variation Cost of Goods rows, category `display_type`/`order`, attribute `order` plus visual `color`/`image`, fulfillment-provider `tracking_url_template`/`icon`, and the provenance/runtime keys declared here. notes.shipping zones & tax rates (custom table: Kept verbatim as the empirical trail that motivated task #93 (this project's convention: append, don't erase history) — see the task #93 note for the real, shipped grammar. wc_shipping_zones/wc_shipping_zone_locations/wc_shipping_zone_methods and wc_tax_rates/wc_tax_rate_locations hold 100% of a shop's shipping-zone and tax-rate configuration — real merchant-authored business rules with zero post/option representation. Stated plainly, verified by reading the engine, not assumed: Capture.php has NO code path that reads ANY custom table into canonical state, for ANY manifest, ever — `Policy::table_rule()` (the only consumer of a manifest's "tables" section) is called exactly once in this codebase, from Journal.php's ground_truth(), purely to score provenance-journal proposals ('managed', i.e. deliberately-out-of-scope, rather than 'unclassified'). It has no effect whatsoever on what `duo capture`/`duo apply` do. So every table below is added to this manifest as an intent marker only — the same honest, no-implementation-behind-it convention manifests/woocommerce.json already established for woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies before this round touched it — NOT a claim of coverage. Empirically characterized column shapes (DESCRIBE against a live WooCommerce 11.0.0 install), precise enough to write the eventual typed-snapshot acceptance criteria from: `wc_shipping_zones` (zone_id PK auto_increment, zone_name, zone_order — no FK-shaped columns of its own, but IS a referenced parent: zone_id is a natural candidate for its own ledger id_kind since two child tables point at it) / `wc_shipping_zone_locations` (location_id PK, zone_id FK -> shipping_zones, location_code a semantic string like 'US' or 'US:CA' — not a ref, location_type) / `wc_shipping_zone_methods` (zone_id FK, instance_id PK auto_increment, method_id a plain string like 'flat_rate'/'free_shipping', method_order, is_enabled). `wc_tax_rates` (tax_rate_id PK auto_increment — a referenced parent for one child table, no FK columns of its own — tax_rate_country/state/rate/name/priority/compound/shipping/order/class, all plain scalars) / `wc_tax_rate_locations` (location_id PK, tax_rate_id FK -> tax_rates, location_code, location_type). The genuinely novel sub-problem, sharper than 'declare column-level refs on a custom table' (DESIGN.md's own framing for typed snapshot): shipping METHOD instance SETTINGS (title/cost/tax_status for flat_rate; min_amount for free_shipping) are NOT columns on wc_shipping_zone_methods at all — they live in `wp_options`, under a name the method instance's own auto-increment id is baked into: `woocommerce_<method_id>_<instance_id>_settings` (confirmed empirically live: creating a flat_rate method on a fresh zone minted `woocommerce_flat_rate_1_settings`; a free_shipping method on the same zone minted `woocommerce_free_shipping_2_settings` — instance_id 1 and 2, this environment's own auto-increment sequence). Three compounding problems, not one: (a) the option's NAME, not just its value, contains an environment-local id, so no `ref`-on-value declaration (the only kind this manifest format has) can fix it; (b) that id is minted by an entirely different table's auto-increment counter, so resolving it needs a ledger lookup keyed by a DIFFERENT entity's identity, a cross-table dependency no current option rule can express; (c) `options` capture is whitelist-only by exact key (`Policy::authored_options()`, read by `Capture::build_options()`) with NO pattern-matching path at all, confirmed by reading the function directly — unlike `attribute_pa_*` above, `option_patterns` exists as a manifest key and IS consulted by `Policy::option_rule()`, but `authored_options()` never calls it, so even a matching option_patterns rule would never cause `build_options()` to discover and read the row; the instance id being unpredictable in advance (it's minted per zone/method, per environment, in creation order) means there is no fixed option NAME a static rule could list either. This shape needs new engine capability on three axes at once (id-in-option-name resolution, cross-table ledger dependency, and a discovery mechanism replacing the exact-key whitelist) before it can even become a manifest-authoring problem — not attempted here; characterized instead so grind round R1-B's acceptance criteria were grounded in what was actually found, not guessed (the task #93 note below is the shipped grammar that answered them).

notes.default_product_cat (DUO-3509): The option `duo pending` demanded a decision for on a fresh WP 7.0.3 + WooCommerce 11.0.1 install, classified authored + ref:term against WooCommerce 11.0.1's own source — and the note carries a keyspace hazard the declaration cannot express. What it is: the product category a product falls back to when it has none, exactly parallel to core.json's own `default_category`. Authored because a human picks it: WC_Admin_Taxonomies::handle_product_cat_row_actions() writes it from the 'Make default' row action (includes/admin/class-wc-admin-taxonomies.php:421) and WC_Install::create_terms() seeds it with the 'Uncategorized' product_cat at install (includes/class-wc-install.php:1639-1658). THE HAZARD, verified by reading every writer and reader rather than assuming: WooCommerce conflates two ID keyspaces on this one option — DESIGN.md 2.2's named failure mode, 'term_id vs term_taxonomy_id ... distinct keyspaces used inconsistently'. Install WRITES a term_taxonomy_id (`absint($default_product_cat->term_taxonomy_id)`, class-wc-install.php:1647, and `absint($result['term_taxonomy_id'])` at :1652), while the admin action WRITES a term_id (`absint($_GET['tag_ID'])`, class-wc-admin-taxonomies.php:421). The readers split the same way: term_id in WC_Admin_Taxonomies::product_cat_notes() (`get_term($category_id, 'product_cat')`, :340) and product_cat_row_actions() (`$default_category_id !== $term->term_id`, :399), and in WC_Post_Data::force_default_term(), which hands it to wp_set_post_terms() — a term-id API (includes/class-wc-post-data.php:670-674); but term_taxonomy_id in AssignDefaultCategory::maybe_assign_default_product_cat(), which INSERTs it straight into wp_term_relationships.term_taxonomy_id (src/Internal/AssignDefaultCategory.php). Duo's ref vocabulary is post|term|user (Policy::set_rule()'s own regex) — there is deliberately no `term_taxonomy` ref; the engine models tt_id only as a deletion guard's `id_kind`, and this manifest's own term:product_cat guards use it there. So `ref: term` resolves through the term-id ledger, which is right for the authoring path and for force_default_term(), and is right for AssignDefaultCategory too on any site where the default category's term_id and term_taxonomy_id coincide — which is every site whose terms were created one-taxonomy-at-a-time by wp_insert_term() (WordPress has split shared terms since 4.4, so the two sequences stay in lockstep). Where they DIVERGE — a database carried forward from a pre-4.4 shared-term site, or one hand-edited — WooCommerce is already inconsistent with itself on this option and no classification can be correct; a divergent site is additionally exposed to Tokens::id_to_token() resolving the stored number as some OTHER term's term_id rather than warning, because a plausible-but-wrong id is indistinguishable from a right one. Declaring it anyway, rather than leaving it pending, is the deliberate call: leaving it undeclared makes every WooCommerce site's `duo init` demand a decision no operator has better evidence for than this note, and the alternative rule (no ref) would carry a raw source-local id into canonical state, which is wrong on every target instead of only a divergent one. Reported to DUO-3509 as an out-of-scope discovery for a keyspace-typed ref, not routed around here.
notes.product_cat_children (DUO-3509): Derived, and the mechanism is WordPress's, not WooCommerce's — grep-confirmed against WooCommerce 11.0.1: no WooCommerce file writes this option at all. It is core's per-taxonomy hierarchy cache, `get_option("{$taxonomy}_children")` in _get_term_hierarchy() (wp-includes/taxonomy.php), which rebuilds it from `get_terms(['fields' => 'id=>parent'])` and update_option()s it whenever the row is missing or not an array; clean_taxonomy_cache() deletes and immediately regenerates it (taxonomy.php:3732-3741), as does _wp_batch_split_terms() for affected taxonomies (:4485). It appears on a WooCommerce site only because WooCommerce registers the hierarchical `product_cat` taxonomy — core's own `category_children` is the identical shape and is likewise undeclared today (reported to DUO-3509 as an out-of-scope discovery; it does not surface on a fresh install because _get_term_hierarchy() only materializes the row once a hierarchy is actually queried). Excluded because its content is a map of THIS environment's term_id => [child term_id] — a foreign environment's id graph is meaningless on a target, and there is nothing authored in it that the term entities Duo already captures do not carry. What `derived` does NOT claim here, stated explicitly per DUO-3509's own question: no Duo rebuilder repairs it. Duo's apply writes terms by hook-free direct SQL and calls neither clean_term_cache() nor clean_taxonomy_cache() (grep-confirmed across agent/src/Apply/), so after an apply that changes the product_cat hierarchy the target's cached row is STALE until WordPress's own next term write invalidates it. That is the same property core.json's `rewrite_rules` carries, and `derived` here means exactly what it means there: excluded from capture and never written by apply, repaired by WordPress's own path rather than by a declared regenerator.
notes.wc_installing / schema-ActionScheduler_*: Two runtime rows the same fresh install surfaced. wc_installing is not a flag but a MUTEX ROW, and it is an option rather than only the same-named transient: WC_Install::create_lock() INSERTs `('wc_installing', <unix time()>, 'no')` with raw SQL specifically so a duplicate-key failure functions as the mutex, then takes the lock over if the stored timestamp is older than ten minutes, and only afterwards sets the backward-compatible transient (includes/class-wc-install.php:713-741); release_lock() DELETEs the row outright (:749-752). A stored `time()` from another environment's install run is meaningless on a target and, if it were replayed while under ten minutes old, would make that target's own WooCommerce installer believe an install is in progress. Runtime. schema-ActionScheduler_LoggerSchema / schema-ActionScheduler_StoreSchema are declared by PATTERN (`^schema-ActionScheduler_`) rather than by their two exact names, because the name is computed: ActionScheduler_Abstract_Schema builds `'schema-' . static::class` in both schema_update_required() and mark_schema_update_complete() (packages/action-scheduler/classes/abstracts/ActionScheduler_Abstract_Schema.php:92, :124), so the two shipped subclasses (classes/schema/ActionScheduler_StoreSchema.php, ActionScheduler_LoggerSchema.php) and any future one are covered by one rule. Runtime rather than env — which is where woocommerce_db_version and woocommerce_schema_version sit — because the VALUE is not a version: mark_schema_update_complete() stores `(string) $this->schema_version . '.0.' . time()` (:124-129), an environment-local timestamp of when THIS install ran the migration, deliberately so ('work around race conditions and ensure that our option updates'). The pattern is deliberately not widened to `^schema-`, which would claim any plugin's schema row; Action Scheduler's own legacy `schema-Action_Scheduler\Custom_Tables\DB_*` names, read at :98-111 only to migrate from the standalone plugin and delete_option()'d on the spot, are left out for the same reason — no site in this project's estate has one, and a rule for a shape nobody has verified is the guess this discipline exists to avoid.
